description: Whether a release statement is structurally valid, checked after the signature and before anything is installed. `accept` means a consumer proceeds to the digest checks; `reject` means it refuses the document. `reason` quotes the rule at issue. These are payloads, not bundles: signature verification is sigstore's and is not restated here.

cases.name: a minimal release statement
two platforms
an unknown field is ignored, not rejected
cases.reason: A later revision of version 1 may add optional fields; an older consumer reads the document anyway.

cases.name: a release that does not pin its signing workflow
cases.comment: pin_workflow is optional and true when absent. false declares that consumers hold later releases to the repository, not the workflow (Reusable workflows).

cases.name: a pin_workflow that is not a boolean
cases.reason: identity.pin_workflow is a boolean; a string is not false.

cases.name: a keyless identity with an empty key_id
cases.reason: key_id is the certificate's subject identity. Both key_id and issuer are required for sigstore-oidc, and neither is empty.

cases.name: a keyless identity with no key_id
cases.reason: identity.key_id is required.

cases.name: a keyless identity with no issuer
cases.reason: identity.issuer is the OIDC issuer, required for sigstore-oidc.

cases.name: a keyless identity with an empty issuer
cases.reason: For sigstore-oidc, key_id is the certificate's subject identity and issuer is the OIDC issuer. Both are required for sigstore-oidc, and neither is empty.

cases.name: extensions carry data the specification does not define
the wrong predicate type
cases.reason: A consumer keeps only the document whose predicateType is release/v1.

cases.name: a version that is not semver
cases.reason: `version` is a semver 2.0.0 version. A consumer refuses anything else; the tag may still be spelled v1.2.

cases.name: a project name with a scheme
cases.reason: A project name is a host with an optional path, with no URL scheme and no trailing slash.

cases.name: a project host with no dot
cases.reason: The host is lowercase and contains at least one dot.

cases.name: an empty path segment in the project name
a project path segment with a tilde
cases.reason: A project name's host is lowercase LDH labels with at least one dot and no port; its path segments use only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `~`, and `-`.

cases.name: a project host with a port
cases.reason: A project name's host is lowercase LDH labels with at least one dot and no port; its path segments use only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `~`, and `-`.

cases.name: a project host label with an underscore
cases.reason: A project name's host is lowercase LDH labels with at least one dot and no port; its path segments use only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `~`, and `-`.

cases.name: a project path segment with a character outside the set
cases.reason: A project name's host is lowercase LDH labels with at least one dot and no port; its path segments use only ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `~`, and `-`.

cases.name: no artifacts
cases.reason: A release statement describes at least one artifact.

cases.name: an artifact that no subject pins
cases.reason: Every artifact must appear in `subject` with its digest, or nothing signs its bytes.

cases.name: two artifacts with the same name
two artifacts a consumer could not choose between
cases.reason: They share os, arch, libc, variant and format, so nothing in the document tells them apart. The vendor must scope or name them differently.

cases.name: a published_at that is not a timestamp
an uppercase token
cases.reason: Vocabulary tokens are lowercase.

cases.name: an executable name that is a path
cases.reason: `bin` names go on PATH; a name cannot contain a separator.

cases.name: an executable with an empty name
cases.reason: A command name is the name as typed, without `.exe`, and is not empty.

cases.name: an executable path that ends in a slash
cases.reason: A command name is not empty, so a string entry's path ends in a file name rather than `/`; `tool/` names no file.

cases.name: requires written as an array
cases.reason: `requires` is an object. An array, even an empty one, is not.

cases.name: an identity written as an array of its fields
cases.reason: `identity` is an object. An array of its values in field order is not.

cases.name: a digest written as an array
cases.reason: `subject[].digest` is an object keyed by algorithm, not an array.

cases.name: a source written as an array
cases.reason: A supplied `source` is an object that includes `repo`, not an array.

cases.name: an executable written as an array of its path and name
cases.reason: A `bin` entry is a path or a `{ path, name }` object, not an array.

cases.name: static completion names one shell
exec completion lists shells and substitutes in argv
exec completion substitutes shells in environment
exec completion cannot use a static single-shell declaration
cases.reason: With exec, shells lists every shell the command generates and {shell} stands for each in the argv or in an env value.

cases.name: exec completion needs a shell placeholder
cases.reason: With exec, shells lists every shell the command generates and {shell} stands for each in the argv or in an env value.
